items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1959-06-02
items.q: I have a copy of that I got from Johnny St. Cyr.

ctx.x: I wouldn't even want him to teach a boy drummer. I even wouldn't do that. I didn't want nothing to do with it. So I never did try to fool with it. I never did try to play. I took one job after I quit and joined church. I used to play there in Baton Rouge, you know, LSU's place. Oh yeah. All the way to play at regular. So the man was so nice to us. And I had my truck. I used to make 25 dollars to haul the band, you see. But I won that 25 dollar. So I took one job and went up there and played it. And I had to sit…

I wondered if you saved any of the old pictures. Do you have that one picture there with Clarence Williams and all. I have a copy of that I got from Johnny St. Cyr. Do you have any other old pictures that you saved from the bands?
Well, I had one I'd give it to my cousin. I had a good picture. Most I got now I did my own pictures. So I got some of them if you want to look at that. Yeah, didn't I?

items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1961-04-07
items.q: INTERVIEWER: You remember Bud Scott and Johnny Saint-Cyr both played those six string bandages? ... INTERVIEWEE: Well all the other played with us played six string.

ctx.x: Mm-hm. He told me he took lessons from Johnny, I didn't know that. He told me, Harry Sushant told me that.

Yeah, maybe he did, because Johnny's always, but Mr. Evans you tell him that now, since you called him, I had forgotten all about him. But he was a very, very fine young fellow, and wherever he'd be. His daddy was nice towards our band. We used to play, it was Jay Day's home then. You know we played one week, we used to go to Jay Day's home, before he opened the stove. And the whole band of us, you know, the drum and everybody, the drummers had a hard time. We used to go all upstairs and everything, all around…
Rigley, did you ever, when you were playing your trombone parts, try to echo the trumpet part or any other part?
